change: POST /api/student/track stops auto-completing exercise-3 and debug on a bare page view, and the guard that should have caught their absence now derives its cases from the activity vocabulary instead of listing three types by hand
_context: WHAT WAS WRONG, and it is bigger than the ten rows that surfaced it.
/track auto-completes any activity type outside GRADED_ON_ARRIVAL, and that
set read ['exercise-1','exercise-2','lab']. exercise-3 and debug were not in
it, so merely OPENING one of those pages wrote completed = 1 with a null
score, before a single button was clicked. 146 -frq pages (the handle alias
for exercise-3) and 53 -debug pages are live, so the exposure is 199 pages.
The ten activities /api/health was reporting are simply the ones a student
has reached so far.
Both are graded exactly like an exercise-1 page, which WAS in the set:
lib/csa-frq-pages.js and lib/csa-debug-pages.js each build a Submit for
grading button posting to /code-grade against hidden test cases, and both
carry a denominator on all 53 CSA lessons, so the gradebook prices them.
WHY IT WAS MISSED, which is the part worth keeping. The set was written on
2026-08-24 against the three types that existed then. exercise-3 was
declared in utils.js that same day; debug entered the gradebook contract on
2026-09-01. smoke/track-visit-completion-guard.js tested the same three
types and stayed green through both additions. A hardcoded list beside a
vocabulary that grows is a list that drifts, and a guard written the same
way cannot tell you it has.
So section 8 of that guard now DERIVES its cases: every activity token a
handle can produce, resolved through the same trailingActivity the route
uses, crossed with isGradedActivity from lib/gradebook-contract.js. A new
activity type fails the suite the day it is added until somebody classifies
it. code and gap are classified as deliberately auto-completing, each with
its reason, so they are decisions on the record rather than omissions.
THERE IS NO live CHECK AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. This change stops a FUTURE
visit from completing graded work. Nothing observable in production moves
when it deploys: the rows already written stay written, so the reporter
count does not drop, and the only way to watch the new behaviour is to post
a visit as a student, which is writing student data to prove a point. A
commit-sha pin would have been a dated receipt rather than a check, which
this repo learned on 2026-09-18. rederive is the honest kind here.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO. The ten rows already carrying completed = 1 with a
null score are historical data. Code cannot clear them and clearing them is
a backfill against student records, which is on the NEVER_AUTO list. They
stay, and /api/health keeps reporting them, until a human decides.

checks.name: a bare visit never completes a graded activity, derived from the vocabulary
checks._why: Sections 1 to 7 are the original hand-written cases, kept because they pin the grading flow and the lesson and quiz paths too. Section 8 is the one that would have caught this: it generates a case per activity token rather than naming three, and asserts the derivation actually reaches exercise-3 and debug so it cannot quietly test nothing.

checks.name: THE EXACT PRE-FIX SET: exercise-3 and debug absent again
checks._why: The defect reproduced. This is the one mutation that matters, because it is not a hypothetical break: it is the code that was serving 199 live pages until today, and the old guard was green against it.

checks.name: only debug is dropped, so the two additions are proven independently
checks._why: Dropping both at once could pass on either assertion alone. Per-rule isolation is the repo convention precisely because a suite going red for a neighbouring reason tells you nothing about the rule you meant to test.

checks.name: the derivation stops reaching anything, so the new section goes hollow
checks._why: The guard this replaces was green because it tested the wrong three things. A derived guard can fail the same way if the derivation silently yields nothing, so the suite asserts it reaches exercise-3 and debug by name. This breaks the derivation to prove that assertion is load bearing.

checks.name: the declared set and the observed behaviour agree on what a visit completes
checks._why: Two paths sharing no code: a TEXT parse of GRADED_ON_ARRIVAL out of routes/student.js, and a POST to /track per activity token against a throwaway database, reading progress.completed back. It catches the failure the suite cannot, because the set DRIVES the behaviour and so a change to the set moves both sides together. What this finds is the linkage breaking: the set consulted too late or not at all, or a type suppressed by something other than the set. Both directions measured against a deliberate break.
checks.expect: the two derivations agree on 5 type(s)
